claims.text: CrCoNi is a high-entropy alloy system.
High-strain-rate loading of CrCoNi generates more deformation twinning than quasi-static loading.
Deformation twinning enables rapid strain accommodation during dynamic loading.
Deformation twinning increases strain hardening in dynamically loaded CrCoNi.
Twinning reconciles high strength with ductility in CrCoNi under dynamic loading.
The proposed test material is annealed, equiaxed, low in initial twin density, and free of significant secondary-phase precipitates.
Twin density and twin distribution are the structural mediators of the strain-rate-dependent response.
CrCoNi has sufficiently low stacking-fault energy to promote deformation-twin nucleation at high strain rates.
Deformation twins provide additional modes of strain accommodation analogous to additional slip systems.
Twin boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby enhance strain hardening.
The combination of twin-mediated strain accommodation and impeded dislocation motion permits continued plastic flow while increasing hardening.
Relative to quasi-static deformation, high-rate deformation will produce a measurable increase in deformation-twin density.
Relative to quasi-static deformation, high-rate deformation will increase strain hardening.
Relative to quasi-static deformation, high-rate deformation will increase ductility.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to single-phase CrCoNi without significant second-phase precipitates.
The proposed mechanism should operate only over temperatures and strain rates for which stacking-fault energy remains low enough to favor twin nucleation.
The applicable temperature range includes near-room temperature and may extend to moderately elevated temperatures.
The relative contributions of twinning and dislocation slip are quantitatively uncertain.
Twin formation may be sensitive to grain size and slight compositional changes.
